guide_description: One day inside and above the walled city: walk the full circuit of the medieval walls at the start of the day before the heat builds, descend into the limestone lanes of the Stradun, and end the evening on a hillside above the rooftops.

days.cluster_tagline: A medieval republic in stone - walls, marble lanes, and Adriatic sea views
days.neighborhood_description: Dubrovnik's Old Town is a fully intact medieval fortified city on a limestone promontory. Nearly every major monument sits within a 2-kilometer perimeter of walls. The city was an independent republic - the Republic of Ragusa - for nearly five centuries, and its dense grid of limestone palaces, churches, and monasteries reflects that civic wealth.

morning.notes: Buy your ticket at the Pile Gate entrance and walk the circuit clockwise - that direction puts the sea views on your left across the full western stretch, saving the best panoramas rather than arriving at them backwards. The full circuit is nearly 2 kilometers and almost entirely exposed; going at opening (8am) is not just a crowd strategy, it cuts the surface temperature of the stone underfoot by several degrees compared to midday.

afternoon.notes: The monastery cloister is one of the finest Romanesque-Gothic transitional spaces in the Adriatic - the double columns with their carved capitals are mostly original and survived the 1667 earthquake that leveled much of the city. The pharmacy inside claims to be among the oldest continuously operating apothecaries in Europe, open since 1317. Walk the Stradun afterward: the main limestone street was repaved after the 1667 earthquake in a single campaign, giving it an unusually uniform Baroque character for a medieval city.

evening.notes: The free-standing fortress on a 37-meter sea cliff just outside the Pile Gate - accessible on your walls ticket or for a small additional fee. The inscription carved above the gate reads 'Non bene pro toto libertas venditur auro' (Freedom is not sold for all the gold in the world), the motto of the Ragusan Republic. The terrace faces due west over open water and catches the last direct light of the day, with the city walls and Pile Gate framing the view behind you.

if_time_permits.notes: The Gothic-Renaissance palace where Ragusa's rector lived during his one-month term of office - he was not permitted to leave the building without state business, a deliberate design to prevent the accumulation of personal power. The atrium courtyard with its Corinthian capitals is the architectural highlight; the museum upstairs holds Ragusan coins, portraits, and furniture from the republic's five-century run.

The cable car climbs 405 meters to the summit of Mount Srd in under four minutes. The view from the top is the only angle from which the full geometry of the Old Town walls, the island of Lokrum, and the Elaphiti islands beyond read simultaneously. Go in the last hour before sunset when the orange light hits the red rooftiles; the lower cable car station is a 10-minute walk north of the Pile Gate.
